study type: Cohort study with independent cross-sectional analyses at two time points
exposure: human milk metal(loid) content (e.g., manganese, zinc, iron, copper, nickel, antimony, vanadium)
outcome: infant gut microbiota profile (e.g., Bifidobacterium genus abundance, Corynebacterium, Veillonella spp., Enterobacter spp., Klebsiella genus abundance, Simpson's diversity)
cohort: 77 mother-infant dyads from the MAMI cohort.
finding: The study found significant correlations between human milk metal(loid) concentrations and infant gut microbiota composition and diversity during early and mature lactation stages, with the Klebsiella genus appearing particularly vulnerable to these fluctuations.
cross-section timing: early transitional stage of lactation and mature stage of lactation
